profile.name: Watney Robotics
profile.summary: San Francisco startup building dual-arm robots for hyperscale data center maintenance: cable replacement, power-cycling servers, reseating parts and inspection. Meta is its publicly reported pilot, with two robots at Altoona, Iowa. These are pilots, not a commercial contract at scale.

pack.title: Hyperion supervised cable-swap pilot
pack.baselineLabel: Estimated technician hours per year on cable and reseat work at full staffing (estimate, not measured)
assumptions: Rule of thumb: 1,000 permanent jobs x 30% hands-on technicians x 15% of time on cable and reseat work x 2,000 hours per year = 90,000 hours.
Only the 1,000 permanent jobs figure is sourced, and it applies at full operation, expected by 2036. The 30%, 15% and 2,000 figures are placeholders for Meta to replace.
No Watney speed or reliability figures are assumed; public reports say tested robots are slower than trained technicians.
pack.successTest: In one data hall, supervised robots take on enough cable swaps to cut technician hands-on hours for that task by {pct}%, with no increase in incidents, against a baseline measured before the pilot.
risks: Robots are publicly reported as slower than trained technicians and need supervision.
Battery limits can force mid-shift recharging.
Hyperion is still being built, so a live hall may not be available at first.
ABB and Kinova are in Meta's pilots too.
The Altoona pilot is not a signed commercial contract at scale.
pack.pathToOrder: Use Altoona results as the reference, agree a measured baseline in one Hyperion hall, run the supervised pilot, then review against the success test before any order for later halls.
